resolution.rationale: Goals are still AIR-only upstream in v0.100.0 and there is no provider-neutral opt-in, so the patch is not absorbed. It replays onto v0.100.0 without conflict and with the ledger's stable patch-id (650615ee), so its added, removed and context lines are unchanged. The v0.99.1..v0.100.0 edits of src/acp-agent.ts (#1474, #1493, #1494, #1495, #1496, #1508, #1509, #1510, #1511) do not touch src/goal-extension.ts, goalMeta, the GOAL_* constants, the v1 _session/goal handler or the publishGoal call site. The #1495 request validation covers relative cwd/additionalDirectories, audio or unknown prompt blocks, set_config_option value types, the authenticate methodId and the session/fork error code; none of it touches initialize, clientCapabilities._meta or the goal method, and a /goal prompt is a text block. The only v0.100.0 docs/air-extensions.md edit rewrites the AIR session/delete bullet, outside the sections the patch edits. #1495 now strips the AIR goal entry from the v2 initialize response; the top-level neutral _meta.goal is still advertised to a v2 client that opts in, which predates this release and does not reach Alas (ACP v1). Reverting the patch on the candidate fails 'advertises and publishes goals for an opted-in non-AIR client'.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts -t goal
npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts -t goal

resolution.rationale: Upstream #1511 wraps the message-loop tool result update in withRunningToolCall(..., runningToolCalls), which keeps a backgrounded Monitor or Workflow call in_progress for v2 sessions that report background work. The v0.98 adaptation replaced the asyncTasks.enabled argument of backgroundedBashToolCall inside that expression, so it conflicted there. The adaptation keeps upstream's withRunningToolCall wrapper and passes the patch's AIR-only clientSupportsAirCapability(this.clientCapabilities, AIR_ASYNC_TASKS_CAPABILITY), so an opted-in v1 client (_meta["async-tasks"]: true) keeps the task lifecycle without the AIR backgrounded marker and v2 keeps upstream's behaviour. Upstream #1495 stopped advertising the AIR asyncTasks capability to v2 because the v2 app registers no _session/async_task/stop; the neutral _meta["async-tasks"] names the same control method, so it is added to UNSERVED_EXTENSION_KEYS in src/v2/initialize.ts, inheriting upstream's v1-only scope. #1510/#1511 background-work reporting is gated to v2 sessions with perTaskStopAffordance, so it does not reach the v1 opt-in. Resolving to upstream's asyncTasks.enabled fails two provider-neutral async-task tests, dropping withRunningToolCall fails upstream's two v2 background tests, and removing the UNSERVED_EXTENSION_KEYS entry fails the new v2 test.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts src/tests/async-tasks.test.ts src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts

resolution.rationale: The patch is stacked on async-tasks-opt-in and its v0.98 copy conflicted only as a cascade of that adaptation. The _alas/context_usage handler, its parameter parsing, the v1 _meta.contextUsage advertisement and the v1 route are unchanged; no v0.100.0 edit touches them (#1484 only adds a usage_update after ExitPlanMode clears context, and the request reads session.query at call time). The adaptation applies #1495's v2 contract to this extension: the v2 app does not register _alas/context_usage, so contextUsage is added to UNSERVED_EXTENSION_KEYS and the v2 initialize response no longer offers a method it cannot serve. Removing that entry fails the new v2 test; disabling the v1 advertisement fails three v1 context-usage tests. Alas uses ACP v1 and is unaffected.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts

resolution.rationale: The v0.98 copy conflicted in docs/air-extensions.md and src/acp-agent.ts only because it wraps and extends the initialize _meta and docs lines of the async-tasks and context-usage patches; onto their adaptations its +/- lines replay unchanged. Upstream v0.100.0 touches the index only through #1495: session/list rejects a relative cwd before anything else, and lists without an index pass includeWorktrees:false. The relative-cwd check runs before SessionIndexConnection.list, so neutral clients get it; the neutral index serves lists itself, so includeWorktrees:false does not apply; and a neutral client takes the service delete path, which keeps answering -32002 for an unknown session, as AIR with sessionIndex does. negotiate still creates no service under v2 and indexCapabilities gained no upstream additions. Two new tests pin these v0.100 contracts; with negotiate ignoring the neutral opt-in, both fail together with eight existing neutral tests.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/session-index.test.ts src/tests/acp-scenarios.test.ts

resolution.rationale: The v0.98 copy conflicted in src/acp-agent.ts only because its opt-in helper sits next to the context-usage helper; onto the adaptation chain its +/- lines replay unchanged. Upstream v0.100.0 does not change endsTurnsWithLiveSubagents, turnAwaitingSubagents or backgroundSubagents, so the opt-in still goes through upstream's single gate, v1 only; #1510/#1511 are v2-only. The adaptation pins a v0.100 contract the patch now relies on, #1494: session/close cancels pending permission requests, elicitations and dialogs before it responds. A settleAtResult client can hold a subagent's permission request outside any turn after its prompt was answered at the result, and that request is now cancelled before close responds. Removing the settleAtResult branch fails the new test and five existing settleAtResult tests; reverting #1494's untilSessionClosed fails the new test and upstream's four close tests.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts -t settleAtResult

resolution.rationale: The carry is a cherry-pick of upstream #1491 (1d2b92fe), which v0.100.0 contains; v0.100.0 then moves to @agentclientprotocol/sdk 2.4.0 (#1509, 720bbb3e). The src +/- lines are identical (normalizeElicitationSchema fills properties: properties ?? {}), as are the harness, elicitation-test and acp-v2-test hunks; the patch-ids differ only because the carry left out upstream's provider-session-configuration.test.ts hunk, whose suite is not in v0.99.1. resolution.rationale: The carry 7f76bbe6 is a git cherry-pick -x of upstream eb78afa8 (#1496, report subagent working directories), which v0.100.0 contains. resolution.rationale: The patch from PR #35 merges cleanly into the v0.100.0 sources: #1495 moved forkSession's body into forkTranscript behind a mapping of the SDK's 'Session <id> not found' to -32002, and the patch's forkPoint parsing sits inside forkTranscript. Its only conflict was in src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts, where its v2 advertisement test and the v0.100 tests for unserved v2 extensions are added at the same place; both are kept. The fork point stays advertised to v2 because the v2 app serves session/fork through unstable_forkSession, so it is not an unserved extension key. A new test pins the v0.100 contract the strict neutral form relies on: a fork point in a session without a transcript fails with -32002 sessionNotFound, not as a fork point that matches no message; it fails when upstream's mapping is disabled. Without the patch's src/fork-session.ts, 36 fork-session tests fail.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/fork-session.test.ts src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts
